blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce \textbf{LoopWAM}, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. On RoboChallenge Table30-V2, three deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 23.67\% to 43.33\%, a 19.7-percentage-point gain, with a final score of 56.80. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5\% average success on RoboTwin~2.0 and 49.5\% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. On challenging shirt folding task, two rounds of deployment-driven improvement after single-task post-training raise success from 13.20\% to 55.56\%. These results demonstrate closed-loop improvement from mixed-quality experience under both multi-task learning and single-task post-training. \href{https://loop-wam.github.io/}{\textcolor{orange}{Project Page}}

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Scaling human-collected robot data has expanded the capabilities of generalist manipulation policies ( O’Neill et al., 2024 ) , but demonstration scaling alone does not close the loop between deployment and continual improvement.
Deployment exposes states, interactions, and failure modes beyond curated demonstrations, providing new experience for an embodied data flywheel.
Real-world reinforcement learning (RL) ( Xu et al., 2026 ) can improve policy performance during deployment, but may narrow the model’s predictive distribution and often struggles to learn multi-task generalist policies.
Although distilling a generalist policy from multiple RL specialists ( Xiao et al., 2025 ) can address this issue, the generalist’s supervision comes from curated successful rollouts rather than the full interaction history.
Therefore, we aim to study direct generalist improvement from the full mixture of successful, suboptimal, and failed deployment rollouts.
The challenge is to use this experience productively: imitating every recorded action risks absorbing undesirable behavior, while retaining only high-quality trajectories discards informative interactions and their outcomes.
blocks.zh:
扩大人类收集的机器人数据扩大了通用主义操纵政策的能力(O ' Neill等人,2024年),但单靠示范规模并不能切断部署与持续改进之间的循环。
部署将暴露在各种状态、互动和失败模式之外,超越了精心设计的演示,为包含的数据飞轮提供了新的经验。
现实世界的强化学习(RL)(徐等人,2026年)在部署期间可以提高政策性能,但可能缩小模型的预测分布,并经常努力学习多任务通用政策.
虽然从多位RL专家(Xiao et al.,2025)中提炼出一种通论政策可以解决这个问题,但通论者的监督来自于整理的成功推出,而不是完整的互动历史.
因此,我们的目标是研究如何从成功、次最佳和失败的部署的完全混合出发,直接改进一般做法。
挑战在于有效地利用这种经验:模仿每一个记录的行动都有可能吸收不良行为,而只保留高质量的轨迹,丢弃信息性互动及其结果。

blocks.en:
Recent VLA and world-action models address important pieces of this problem.
On the VLA side, π 0.6 \pi_{0.6} ( Physical Intelligence, 2025 ) uses advantage-conditioned learning to incorporate autonomous experience and interventions, while π 0.7 \pi_{0.7} ( Physical Intelligence, 2026 ) uses quality, speed, and mistake metadata to absorb mixed-quality data and distill specialist capabilities into a generalist.
These VLA methods use steering during training to model behavior distributions across data qualities and specify a desirable mode at inference for smooth execution, but rely on VLM-based language–vision–action representations without an explicit objective for learning the physical dynamics reflected in action–video transitions.
Consequently, suboptimal and failed rollouts provide behavior targets but do not directly supervise learning of their physical consequences.
World modeling offers a more elegant solution: WAMs ( Pai et al., 2025 ; Ye et al., 2026b ; Li et al., 2026 ) couple predictive visual representations with action generation, while action-conditioned world models (ACWMs) ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Gao et al., 2026 ) predict future observations conditioned on actions.
Combining the two allows ACWM to learn action consequences from data of different qualities, while WAM learns appropriate actions from expert demonstrations. τ 0 \tau_{0} -WM ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) trains separate WAM and ACWM, routing failure and recovery data to ACWM training and use ACWM as selector for policy improvement.
FACT ( Peng et al., 2026 ) implements the two roles within a shared model, but retains sequential action–consequence generation. It only supports success/failure supervision split, with failure consequences influencing the policy implicitly through shared representations.
These approaches expose a remaining design challenge in learning from mixed-quality deployment experience: VLA steering lacks natural action–video dependency modeling, while consequence-aware WAMs still exploit rollout data indirectly through an ACWM interface—a simulator for action selection or a subsequent consequence-prediction stage that influences the policy through shared representations.
Can a single WAM directly learn from mixed-quality deployment rollouts, with all qualities supervising the model and learned consequences participating directly in action generation?
blocks.zh:
最近《志愿行动法》和世界行动模式处理了这一问题的重要部分。
在VLA方面,^ 0.6\pi_{0.6}(物理智能,2025年)利用优势条件的学习来吸收自主经验和干预,而^ 0.7\pi_{0.7}(物理智能,2026年)则利用质量,速度和错误的元数据来吸收混合质量的数据,将专家能力提炼成通论者.
这些VLA方法在训练期间使用指导来模拟跨数据质量的行为分布,并指定一个可取的推论模式,以便顺利执行,但依赖于基于VLM的语言-视觉-动作表达,而没有明确的目标来学习动作-视频转换中反映的物理动态.
因此,不良和失败的推出提供了行为目标,但并不直接监督其物理后果的学习。
世界建模提供了一个更优雅的解决方案:WAMs(Pai等人,2025年;Ye等人,2026年b;Li等人,2026年b)将预测视觉表现与动作生成结合,而动作有条件的世界模型(ACWMs)(Guo等人,2025年;Gao等人,2026年b)预测未来以动作为条件的观测.
两者的结合使得ACWM能够从不同品质的数据中学习行动后果,而WAM则从专家演示中学习适当的行动. 0\tau_{0}-WM(周 al等人,2026年)列车将WAM和ACWM分开,向ACWM培训的路由故障和恢复数据,并使用ACWM作为政策改进的选择器.
FACT(Peng等人,2026年)在一个共同的模式中执行这两个角色,但保留了顺序动作-后果生成. 它只支持成功/失败监督的分裂,失败后果通过共同陈述间接影响政策。
这些方法暴露了在学习混合质量部署经验方面仍然存在的设计挑战: VLA引导缺乏自然行动-视频依赖性模型,而后果意识的WAM仍然通过ACWM接口间接地利用推出数据——作为行动选择的模拟器或随后通过共享表述影响政策的后果预测阶段。
一个WAM能否直接从混合质量的部署推广中吸取教训,所有素质都监督模型,学到的后果直接参与行动生成?

blocks.en:
We introduce LoopWAM , a closed-loop World-Action Model that updates a generalist directly from mixed-quality deployment rollouts.
Our core idea is to let one WAM directly absorb rollouts across the full quality spectrum and learn from each.
To achieve this, we first use source-dependent noise sampling to unify WAM behavior learning and ACWM consequence learning within a single model and generation stage.
Video and action noise levels are sampled independently, allowing low-noise rollout actions to guide prediction of their observed consequences.
Within this unified model, quality steering represents behaviors of different qualities and selects the highest-quality condition at deployment.
To control how strongly each behavior is imitated, we further apply quality-weighted supervision , reducing imitation of suboptimal actions and masking failed-action targets while retaining video supervision across all qualities.
Together, these mechanisms let every trajectory supervise the joint model according to its behavioral quality and observed transitions.
Video and action tokens interact bidirectionally throughout one parallel denoising process, allowing learned future representations to participate in action formation without a separate consequence-evaluation stage.
We close the loop by repeatedly collecting rollouts and retraining the generalist on demonstrations and accumulated experience before redeployment.
On RoboChallenge Table30-V2 ( RoboChallenge Dexmal Team, 2026 ) , three rounds raise overall success from 23.67% to 28.00% , 37.67% , and 43.33% , a 19.7-percentage-point improvement , with a final score of 56.80 , ranking first in both success and score among the compared entries (Table 1 ).
LoopWAM achieves 94.5% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 ( Chen et al., 2025 ) , exceeding the reported 87.5% of FACT and 93.6% of LingBot-VA 2.0, and 49.5% on the 50-task RoboCasa365 evaluation ( Nasiriany et al., 2026 ) , above ABot-M0.6’s 46.6% (Tables 2 – 3 ).
We further evaluate deployment-driven self-improvement after single-task post-training on challenging shirt folding, which involves deformable objects and multiple coordinated steps.
Two deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 13.20% to 55.56% (Section 4.4 ).
These results establish that directly learning from mixed-quality rollouts with parallel world–action denoising can deliver leading benchmark performance and repeated deployment improvement in both multi-task and single-task settings.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了LoopWAM, 即一个闭路世界行动模式,
我们的核心思想是让一个WAM直接吸收整个质量范围的推出,并从中学习。
为了实现这一目标,我们首先使用依赖源的噪声取样,将WAM行为学习和ACWM后果学习统一在一个模型和生成阶段.
视频与动作噪声水平是独立取样的,允许低噪声的展开动作来指导对其观察到的后果的预测.
在这个统一的模型中,质量引导代表不同品质的行为,并在部署时选择最高质量的条件.
为了控制每个行为被模仿的程度,我们进一步运用质量加权监督,减少模仿次最佳行动,掩盖失败行动目标,同时保留所有质量的视频监督.
这些机制使每个轨迹都能够根据其行为质量和观察到的转变来监督联合模型。
视频和行动符号在整个平行的解密过程中进行双向互动,使学到的今后表述能够在没有单独的后果评价阶段的情况下参与行动形成。
我们通过反复收集推广和再培训关于示威和在重新部署前积累经验的通论家来结束这一循环。
在RoboChallenge Table30-V2(RoboChallenge Dexmal Team,2026年)上,三轮将总体成功率从23.67%提升到28.00 %,37.67%,43.33%,以19.7个百分点的成绩提高,最终得分56.80分,在比较分中均排名第一(表1).
LoopWAM在RoboTwin 2.0(Chen等人,2025年)上取得了94.5%的平均成功,超过了所报道的87.5%的FACT和93.6%的LingBot-VA 2.0,以及49.5%的RoboCasa365评价(Nasiriany等人,2026年),高于ABot-M0.6的46.6%(表2-3)。
我们进一步评价在就挑战性衬衫折叠问题进行单一任务后培训后部署驱动的自我改进,这涉及可变形物体和多个协调步骤。
两轮部署和训练将成功率从13.20%提高到55.56%(第4.4节)。
这些结果确定,从与平行世界的混合质量推广中直接学习,在多任务和单一任务环境下,消除行动可以提供领先的基准业绩和反复部署改进。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Robot Manipulation Policies. Robot manipulation policies increasingly combine scalable imitation learning with pretrained representations.
ACT ( Zhao et al., 2023 ) and Diffusion Policy ( Chi et al., 2025 ) learn action sequences from demonstrations, while RT-2 ( Zitkovich et al., 2023 ) and OpenVLA ( Kim et al., 2024 ) transfer vision-language priors to language-conditioned control.
Flow-based policies such as π 0 \pi_{0} ( Black et al., 2024 ) and π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Physical Intelligence et al., 2025 ) further scale continuous action generation and generalization.
Open X-Embodiment ( O’Neill et al., 2024 ) and DROID ( Khazatsky et al., 2024 ) expand training coverage across embodiments and environments.
Beyond offline demonstrations, DAgger ( Ross et al., 2011 ) addresses policy-induced distribution shift by collecting expert labels on visited states.
LoopWAM studies learning from the recorded observations and actions of deployment rollouts, using trajectory quality to guide policy updates while retaining world supervision from unsuccessful interactions.
blocks.zh:
机器人操纵政策. 机器人操纵政策越来越多地将可伸缩的仿真学习与预先训练过的表述相结合.
ACT(Zhao等人,2023年)和传播政策(Chi等人,2025年)从演示中学习动作序列,而RT-2(Zitkovich等人,2023年)和OpenVLA(Kim等人,2024年)则将视觉语言前传转移到语言条件控制.
以流动为基础的政策,如 ^ 0\pi_{0}(Black等人, 2024年)和 ^ 0.5\pi_{0.5) (物理情报等人, 2025年) 进一步扩大连续行动生成和概括。
开放X-Embodiment(O ' Neill等人,2024年)和DROID(Khazatsky等人,2024年)将培训涵盖范围扩大,涵盖各种表现形式和环境。
Dagger(Ross等人,2011年)在离线演示之外,通过收集受访国家的专家标签,解决政策引起的分销转移问题。
LoopWAM研究从记录的观察和部署推广行动中学习,利用轨迹质量指导政策更新,同时保留对不成功互动的世界监督.

blocks.en:
World Action Models. Video-based robot policies use predictive visual representations to support control.
mimic-video ( Pai et al., 2025 ) conditions an action decoder on representations from a pretrained video model.
DreamZero ( Ye et al., 2026b ) jointly generates video and actions, while LingBot-VA ( Li et al., 2026 ) organizes visual prediction and action decoding within a causal autoregressive framework.
LingBot-VA 2.0 ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) further develops native video-action pretraining with a control-oriented tokenizer.
Efficiency-oriented designs include Fast-WAM ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) , which retains video co-training but removes future-video generation at inference, and GigaWorld-Policy ( Ye et al., 2026a ) , which learns action-conditioned visual dynamics while allowing action-only inference.
Being-H0.7 ( Luo et al., 2026 ) instead uses future observations to supervise latent representations.
These studies establish several ways for predictive supervision to support action learning.
LoopWAM focuses on closing the deployment–training loop: mixed-quality rollouts broaden world-model training, while joint video–action modeling, quality steering, and weighted action supervision connect consequence awareness with high-quality behavior.
blocks.zh:
世界行动模式。 基于视频的机器人政策使用预测的视觉表现支持控制.
模拟视频 (Pai等人,2025年)为预训视频模型的表达设置了动作解码器.
DreamZero(Ye et al., 2026b)联合生成视频和动作,而LingBot-VA(Li et al., 2026)则在一个因果自递式框架内组织视觉预测和动作解码.
LingBot-VA 2.0 (Zhang et al., 2026a)进一步开发了以控制为导向的标致器的本土视频动作预训.
效率导向的设计包括Fast-WAM(Yuan等人,2026年),它保留了视频协同训练,但在推论中取消了未来的视频生成,以及GigaWorld-Policy(Ye等人,2026a年),它学习了行动有条件的视觉动态,同时允许只行动推论.
Being-H0.7(Luo等人,2026年)转而利用未来的观察来监督潜在的表述。
这些研究确定了若干预测性监督方法,以支持行动学习。
LoopWAM专注于关闭部署-培训循环:混合质量的推出扩展了世界模式培训,而联合视频-行动模型、质量指导和加权行动监督将后果意识与高质量行为联系起来。

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
LoopWAM learns a world–action model that can be updated with experience collected during deployment.
The framework couples video and action generation within a shared denoising process, then uses trajectory quality to distinguish how deployment data supervise world modeling and control.
Figure 2 summarizes the architecture and training procedure.
We first introduce joint world–action modeling, followed by quality-aware learning from mixed trajectories and the deployment–learning loop.

Quality steering. Within this unified training scheme, each trajectory is assigned a numerical quality score q q , which is shared by all training segments extracted from it.
We encode quality as a suffix to the instruction, ℓ q = [ ℓ ; Quality: q ] \ell_{q}=[\ell;\texttt{Quality:}\ q] , and use its text embeddings to condition both video and action streams.
We support two trajectory annotation schemes: (1) Episode-level annotation , where human annotators or a vision-language model (VLM) score each trajectory individually for fine-grained quality estimation; and (2) coarse-level annotation , where a single human-provided score is assigned to all rollouts from a policy checkpoint based on its overall success rate and motion smoothness.
Under coarse annotation, successful trajectories receive the checkpoint score while failed trajectories receive the minimum score, requiring only one annotation per checkpoint.
Both schemes represent rollout quality using numerical scores.
For expert demonstrations, we assign an expert score q ⋆ q^{\star} that is higher than the maximum rollout quality score.
The quality-conditioned instruction allows different behaviors under the same task instruction to be represented within one model.
During deployment, we condition on q = q ⋆ q=q^{\star} to steer sampling toward expert-quality behavior.

More broadly, LoopWAM’s self-improvement updates can use rollouts from arbitrary deployed policies, even poorly performing ones.
The joint architecture and quality-aware objective accommodate their varying trajectory qualities, so each trajectory contributes according to its observed transitions and behavioral quality.
This extends self-improvement to learning from deployment experience collected by other policies as well as LoopWAM itself.
We validate this broader setting on RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa365 (Section 4.3 ).

blocks.en:
We initialize the video backbone, text encoder, and video VAE from Wan2.2-TI2V-5B ( Wan et al., 2025 ) , and use an action DiT with a hidden dimension of 1024.
Each training segment pairs a 64-step action chunk with nine RGB frames sampled at intervals of eight control steps, including the initial observation.
Multi-camera views are stitched into a single image, and actions and robot states are normalized using expert-data statistics.
Training follows the quality-conditioned joint objective in Section 3.2 , and deployment uses the expert score q ⋆ q^{\star} .
Table30-V2 uses relative joint targets and absolute gripper commands.
Additional training, preprocessing, and subtask-segmentation details are provided in Appendix A .

blocks.en: 4.2 Benchmark Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.2 基准实验设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate LoopWAM on the real-robot benchmark RoboChallenge Table30-V2 and two simulation benchmarks, RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa365.
RoboChallenge evaluates closed-loop self-improvement using LoopWAM’s own real-robot deployments.
The two simulation benchmarks additionally test learning from different deployed policies by augmenting expert demonstrations with rollouts from both expert-trained LoopWAM and others.
Across these settings, successful, suboptimal, and failed rollouts expand the state–action–outcome distribution beyond expert demonstrations.
blocks.zh:
我们用RoboTwin 2.0和RoboCasa365这两个模拟基准来评价RoopWAM。
RoboChallenge使用LoopWAM自己的真机器人部署来评价闭路自我改进.
这两项模拟基准还测试了从不同部署政策中学习的情况,办法是通过推出经过专家培训的LooperWAM和其他方法,加强专家示范。
在这些环境下,成功、次优和失败的推出将国家-行动-结果的分布扩展到专家示威之外。

blocks.en:
RoboChallenge Table30-V2 ( RoboChallenge Dexmal Team, 2026 ) is a standardized real-robot benchmark comprising 30 tabletop manipulation tasks across four embodiments: ALOHA, DOS-W1, ARX5, and UR5.
Its tasks test capabilities including tool use, precise manipulation, and coordinated bimanual control.
We follow the official multi-task evaluation protocol and report overall performance across embodiments.
Starting from one expert-trained multi-task LoopWAM per embodiment, we conduct three successive rounds of closed-loop self-improvement.
In each deployment round, we run each model on its assigned tasks and collect about 100 rollout trajectories per task.
These trajectories are quality-annotated and combined with expert demonstrations and rollout trajectories from all previous deployment rounds for further training.

其任务测试能力包括工具使用,精确操纵,以及协调双人控制.
我们遵循正式的多任务评价程序,并报告各表现的整体业绩。

blocks.en:
RoboTwin 2.0 ( Chen et al., 2025 ) comprises 50 bimanual manipulation tasks evaluated in clean and domain-randomized scenes.
Following the multi-task setup of LingBot-VA ( Li et al., 2026 ) , we use 2,500 expert demonstrations from clean scenes and 25,000 from heavily randomized scenes.
We augment these demonstrations with rollouts generated by expert-trained LoopWAM, X-VLA ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) , and π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Physical Intelligence et al., 2025 ) .
For each task, each policy contributes 20 clean and 130 randomized rollouts, yielding 22,500 trajectories across all 50 tasks and the three policies.
The combined rollout corpus has approximately the same total duration as the expert corpus.
Rollout collection and evaluation use different random seeds to avoid data leakage.
Rollout quality is annotated using the coarse-level numerical scores in Section 3.2 .

blocks.en:
RoboCasa365 ( Nasiriany et al., 2026 ) is a large-scale simulation framework for household manipulation in diverse kitchen environments.
We evaluate on its 50-task benchmark, which includes atomic and composite manipulation tasks.
Training combines expert demonstrations with rollouts generated by expert-trained LoopWAM and RLDX-1 ( Kim et al., 2026 ) , with the combined rollout duration approximately matching that of the expert data.
Both expert and rollout data follow the Human300 training split: the 16 Composite-Unseen tasks are excluded from training and evaluated zero-shot.
As in RoboTwin 2.0, training and evaluation data use different random seeds.

blocks.en:
Table 1 compares expert-trained and final LoopWAM with leading entries from the official leaderboard ( RoboChallenge, 2026 ) .
After three deployment-and-training rounds, LoopWAM attains an overall score of 56.80 and 43.33% success, exceeding VLA-DM0.5 by 2.38 score points and 2.67 percentage points in success, and ranking first on both metrics among the compared methods.

Without additional embodied pretraining, it improves over AHA-WAM by 1.70 percentage points and surpasses the pretrained LingBot-VA 2.0 by 0.90 points on average.

We examine deployment-driven improvement in two real-robot settings: multi-task learning and single-task post-training (Figure 3 ).
Both follow the update procedure in Section 3.3 : the current policy collects rollouts, which are quality-annotated and combined with expert demonstrations and accumulated deployment trajectories for the next update.

我们审查了在两个真正的机器人环境中由部署驱动的改进:多任务学习和单一任务培训后(图3)。
两者都遵循第3.3节的更新程序:现行政策收集推广内容,这些内容附有质量说明,并结合专家演示和累积部署轨迹进行下一次更新。

blocks.en:
Multi-task deployment. As in Section 4.2 , we train multi-task models for ALOHA, DOS-W1, ARX5, and UR5, covering the 30 Table30-V2 tasks.
Starting from expert-trained checkpoints, each model undergoes three rounds of deployment and training using experience from its assigned tasks.
Overall success increases from 23.67% to 28.00%, 37.67%, and 43.33%, while the scores rise from 36.10 to 42.63, 51.65, and 56.80.
Both aggregate metrics improve at every iteration, yielding a 19.7-percentage-point success gain over the initial deployment.
This demonstrates that LoopWAM can use its own deployment experience to improve policies trained across multiple tasks.
blocks.zh:
多任务部署. 如同第4.2节一样,我们为ALOHA、DOS-W1、ARX5和UR5培训多任务模式,涵盖30个表30-V2任务。

这表明,LoopWAM可以利用自己的部署经验,改进在多项任务中培训的政策。

blocks.en:
Single-task post-training. We further evaluate shirt folding, a challenging deformable-object manipulation task that requires multiple coordinated steps.
We initialize from the DOS-W1 multi-task model trained on Table30-V2 and post-train it on newly collected expert demonstrations of shirt folding.
The resulting task-specific expert-trained checkpoint serves as the starting point for two rounds of deployment and self-improvement.
Success rises from 13.20% to 32.54% and 55.56%, while the scores increase from 14.44 to 38.89 and 67.78.
These gains show that deployment feedback remains useful after adapting a multi-task model to a challenging individual task, supporting closed-loop improvement under both training regimes.

blocks.zh: 表4:关于RoboTwin2.0的读物研究. 我们用不同的注释计划来评价质量指导,并评估质量加权推出行动监督的效果(法案)。

blocks.en:
Table 4 compares no steering, extra-coarse annotation, and our coarse-level annotation (Section 3.2 ).
Extra-coarse annotation distinguishes rollouts from all policies solely by success or failure: all failed rollouts are assigned Quality: low , all successful rollouts are assigned Quality: medium , and expert demonstrations are assigned Quality: high .
In our coarse-level scheme, successful rollouts from the same policy are assigned a shared numerical score, which can differ across policies according to their overall success rates across tasks and manually assessed motion smoothness.
Failed rollouts are assigned the minimum score, while expert demonstrations are assigned q ⋆ q^{\star} , above the rollout score range. The ablation results reveal three key findings: (1) Quality steering is key to learning from mixed-quality deployment rollouts, enabling the model to distinguish trajectories of different quality. (2) Even extra-coarse labels remain effective, demonstrating that fine-grained annotation is not required to benefit from steering. (3) Quality-aware rollout action supervision further improves overall performance under both annotation schemes.

粗体外注解将推出与所有政策完全区分为成功或失败:所有失败推出都被指定为质量:低,所有成功推出被指定为质量:中,专家演示被指定为质量:高.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented LoopWAM for improving generalist world-action policies directly from deployment experience.
The key is to learn physical consequences from trajectories across the quality spectrum while controlling how their actions supervise behavior.
Source-dependent noise sampling, quality steering, and quality-weighted supervision implement this distinction within joint video–action denoising, allowing consequence representations to participate directly in action generation.
The same formulation accepts rollouts from both LoopWAM and other deployed policies. Experiments show the best overall results: a score of 56.80 and 43.33% success on RoboChallenge Table30-V2, 94.5% average success on RoboTwin 2.0, and 49.5% overall success on RoboCasa365.
Repeated real-robot deployment raises Table30-V2 success by 19.7 percentage points over three rounds and improves shirt-folding success from 13.20% to 55.56% over two rounds after single-task post-training.
These findings support using mixed-quality interaction history as a training resource for continued improvement of both multi-task policies and policies adapted to individual tasks.
blocks.zh:
我们提出LoopWAM,以便直接根据部署经验改进普遍世界行动政策。
关键在于从质量谱的轨迹中学习物理后果,同时控制他们的行为如何监督行为.
依赖源的噪音取样、质量指导和质量加权监督在联合视频-动作解密中实施这种区分,允许后果表达直接参与动作生成。
同样的表述方式接受LoopWAM和其他已部署政策的推出。 实验显示总体成绩最好:在RoboChallenge Table30-V2上得分56.80%和43.33%,在RoboTwin 2.0上得分平均为94.5%,在RoboCasa365上得分总体为49.5%。
重复的真机器人部署使Table30-V2在三轮试训中的成功率提高了19.7个百分点,并在单轮试训后将穿衬衫的成功率从13.20%提高到55.56%.
这些调查结果支持利用混合质量互动历史作为培训资源,继续改进多任务政策和适合具体任务的政策。

blocks.en: A.2 Training Details
blocks.zh: A.2 培训细节

blocks.en:
Temporal alignment and robot representations. The training configurations use an action horizon of H = 64 H=64 and a visual stride of eight control steps, yielding nine RGB frames including the initial observation.
Camera views are stitched into a single image, and robot states and actions are normalized using expert-data statistics.
For Table30-V2, joint targets are represented relative to the joint state at the beginning of each action chunk, whereas gripper commands remain absolute.
Only the joint components are converted back to absolute targets at execution; the gripper components are not differenced.
To reduce redundant stationary data, the real-world pipeline checks unnormalized state sequences with an absolute tolerance of 10 − 3 10^{-3} and resamples nearly static windows up to three times.
Windows starting within the final 20 seconds of expert episodes are exempt from this filtering to retain terminal behavior.
Padding is excluded from the denoising losses.

blocks.en:

imperfect perception, inaccurate execution, and complex object
interaction dynamics.

互动动态。

该模型在观察所形成的环境状态后生成

环境转型超越了对孤立行动的预测.
